paragraphs: The 82-0 Basketball Builder is an independent roster-building game about one impossible basketball question: could your five-player lineup finish a full season undefeated?

Pick a playstyle, draft one player at a time from different teams and eras, then run the season simulation. Basketball fans love debating whether any roster could survive a full season without a loss — some lineups chase 82W–0L, while others fall short on defense, size, playmaking, or balance. The fun is seeing how your five performs once the full season is projected.

Each round gives you a random team and era. Choose one player from the available pool and place him into an open position on your lineup. Your playstyle controls the shape of the roster: balanced, small ball, twin towers, or run and gun.

You can draft with full stat lines visible, or turn stats off and rely on memory and instinct. After five picks, the simulator projects your roster across an 82-game season and gives you a final record, grade, strengths, and weaknesses.

The simulation engine aggregates your lineup's five statistical categories — scoring, rebounding, playmaking, steals, and blocks — and runs the total through a non-linear win curve. The relationship between stats and wins is not linear: as your team gets stronger, each additional win becomes significantly harder to earn. Going from 70 to 75 wins takes far more roster strength than going from 55 to 60.

On top of the curve, every category is gated. A deficiency in even one area — no rim protection, no playmaking — caps your ceiling and kills the perfect season, no matter how high your scoring total is. And different decades have different statistical environments: 30 points per game in the fast-paced 1960s is not worth the same as 30 in the 2020s, and the engine era-adjusts every stat line accordingly.

The 82-0 challenge rules are simple. One: each round, the slot machine assigns a random team and decade. Two: pick exactly one player from that roster. Three: place him at an open court position he actually played — PG, SG, SF, PF, or C. Four: you have one team skip and one era skip for the whole game. Five: after five picks, the engine simulates your season and projects a final record between 0-82 and 82-0, with a letter grade, your best pick, and your roster's biggest weakness. Share it and challenge your friends to beat it.

sections.h2: Tips to Build a Better Team
paragraphs: Maximize totals across all five categories. The engine has no synergy penalties — it rewards raw, era-adjusted production. But remember the gates: a lineup with zero blocks or zero playmaking caps your ceiling no matter how much it scores.

Mind your positions. Every pick must fit an open court slot the player actually played. Drafting a wing early at small forward can lock you out of a better wing later — keep your remaining slots in mind before you commit.
Know your eras. A 25-point scorer from the 2000s often beats a 30-point scorer from the 1960s after era adjustment. Pace-inflated numbers from older decades are quietly deflated by the engine.
Spend skips early, not late. If round one hands you a thin roster, skip immediately. Saving both skips for round five usually means wasting them.
Want a real test? Play Blind Draft mode — stats are hidden and you draft entirely from memory. It is the fastest way to find out who actually knows basketball history.

If you enjoy this game, you'll probably like other draft-style sports games — lineup builders, era debates, GOAT brackets, and fantasy drafts all scratch the same itch. The format runs for other sports too: 20-0 for the NFL, 38-0 for Premier League soccer, and 7-0 for the World Cup. What sets this one apart is that it gives every roster a clear, simulated result instead of an endless argument — your team either goes undefeated or it doesn't, and there's always another run.

whatIs.title: What Is 82-0? The Perfect NBA Season, Explained
whatIs.description: 82-0 means winning all 82 regular-season games — something no NBA team has ever done. The closest runs, the math that makes it nearly impossible, and the game it inspired.
whatIs.h1: What Is 82-0? The Perfect Season, Explained
whatIs.intro: 82-0 is the perfect NBA regular season: 82 games, 82 wins, zero losses. No team in league history has ever done it — and the numbers explain why it may never happen. This page covers the concept, the closest real-world attempts, and the simulation game built around the question.

paragraphs: Since the 1967-68 season, an NBA regular season has been 82 games long, played from roughly late October to mid-April. A team that went 82-0 would have won every single one of them — every road back-to-back, every night the star sat out, every January game against a team with nothing to lose. The record has become shorthand for an unreachable standard of perfection, which is exactly what makes it fun to argue about.

The phrase shows up constantly in basketball debates: “That lineup would go 82-0.” It is almost never meant literally. It is a way of saying a roster has no weakness worth naming — and the whole point of this site is to put that claim to the test.

sections.h2: How Close Has a Real Team Come?
paragraphs: The best regular season in NBA history belongs to the 2015-16 Golden State Warriors, who went 73-9 — and even they opened with a record 24 straight wins before losing. The 1995-96 Chicago Bulls went 72-10 and won the title. The 1971-72 Los Angeles Lakers won 33 games in a row, still the longest winning streak in major American pro sports, and finished 69-13. The 2012-13 Miami Heat ran off 27 straight.

Notice the pattern: the greatest teams ever assembled, at their absolute peak, still lost nine or more games. The 73-9 Warriors dropped games to lottery teams on the second night of back-to-backs. An 82-0 season would need everything those teams had, plus six months of uninterrupted health and better luck than any team has ever received.

sections.h2: The Math of a Perfect Season
paragraphs: The arithmetic is what kills it. Suppose a team is so dominant it wins any given game 95% of the time — a level no real team has sustained. The chance of doing that 82 times in a row is 0.95 to the 82nd power: about 1.5%. Even a fantasy team that wins each game 99% of the time completes the perfect season less than half the time. Eighty-two is simply a brutal number of coin flips to sweep.

That is why the simulation on this site treats 82-0 the way reality would: a lineup must max out every statistical category to even become eligible, and then still has to survive a final luck roll. Perfect rosters lose sometimes. That is the game.

The 82-0 Challenge turns the debate into something playable. Five rounds of random team-and-era draws, one pick per round, and a season simulation at the end that grades your five across points, rebounds, assists, steals, and blocks — with every stat era-adjusted so a 1960s big man and a 2020s guard are judged on the same scale. Most runs end somewhere in the 60s or 70s. A genuine 82-0 is rare enough that people share screenshots.

If you want to understand exactly how the engine projects wins, read How It's Calculated. If you want to argue about whether any five could do it, the Can You Go 82-0 page walks through the strategy. And if you would rather skip the randomness and hand-pick a dream team, the free-pick Lineup Builder simulates any five you like.

daily.sameDraw: Same draw for every player worldwide

paragraphs: Every day at midnight UTC, a new challenge is generated from the date itself: the five team-and-era draws are derived from a deterministic seed, so a player in Tokyo, a player in Paris, and a player in Chicago all face exactly the same spins in the same order. There are no skips in daily mode — the draw you see is the draw everyone gets — and your finished record can be submitted to the daily leaderboard under any name you choose, no account needed.

You get one attempt per day, tracked on your device. When you finish, the game shows your record and a share text stamped with today's date, so a friend can open the same challenge and try to beat you on identical terms. At midnight UTC the seed rolls over and challenge number, spins, and leaderboard start fresh.

In the classic mode you can replay forever, and that is the point — fishing for a dream draw is half the fun. The daily flips that: because everyone gets the same spins, a record is only comparable if everyone also gets the same number of tries. One attempt makes your 61-21 mean something against your friend's 58-24. No retries also changes how it feels to play: every pick is permanent, so the five decisions carry real weight.

The one-attempt rule lives in your browser rather than behind a login — this site has no accounts. Clearing site data technically resets it, but there is no prize pool here; the only thing at stake is whether your bragging rights are honest.

sections.h2: Daily vs. Classic: A Different Skill
paragraphs: Classic rewards patience across many runs — era knowledge, category balance, and knowing when to burn a skip. The daily is a test of adaptation: you cannot reroll a bad franchise or dodge a thin decade, so the skill is squeezing the strongest five out of whatever the date hands you. A weak draw day is the great equalizer — everyone is building from the same scraps, and the leaderboard shows who adapted best.

Seasoned players treat the two modes differently: in classic they chase the perfect 82-0; in the daily they chase the best possible record for that specific draw, which some days simply is not 82-0. Recognizing the ceiling of a draw — and building to hit it — is its own game.

Since there are no skips, think a step ahead: before locking your first pick, glance at which positions the candidate pool covers and leave yourself an escape hatch for the positions that are hardest to fill — rim protection and rebounding tend to be the scarcest categories late in a draft. The simulation gates every category, so a lineup of four scorers and no boards will cap out in the sixties no matter how pretty the points column looks.

Remember that every stat line is era-adjusted: a 1960s rebounding monster is not being flattered by pace — his number is scaled before it enters the engine. Cross-era fives are judged fairly, so draft the player, not the decade.

howItsCalculated.title: How Is 82-0 Calculated? The Scoring Engine Explained
howItsCalculated.description: How does the 82-0 challenge calculate your record? A plain-English breakdown of the five stat categories, the non-linear win curve, era adjustment, and why one weakness tanks a perfect season.
howItsCalculated.intro: Wondering how the 82-0 challenge turns five players into a win-loss record? Here is exactly what the simulation engine does, in plain English.

paragraphs: After you draft five players, the engine adds up their per-game stats across five categories — points, rebounds, assists, steals and blocks — adjusts every line for the era it came from, then runs the total through a non-linear win curve to project a record between 0-82 and 82-0. A single weak category caps your ceiling no matter how strong the rest of the roster is.

Every player carries a real historical stat line: points (PPG), rebounds (RPG), assists (APG), steals (SPG) and blocks (BPG) per game. The engine sums each category across your starting five, so a lineup's scoring total is the sum of five scorers, its rebounding total the sum of five rebounders, and so on. Balance across all five matters more than a huge number in any one.
This is why a five-scorer lineup underperforms: it piles up points but posts near-zero blocks and playmaking, and the engine punishes that imbalance.

Total stat output does not translate to wins in a straight line. The engine runs your aggregate through a curve where each additional win costs progressively more roster strength. Going from 55 to 60 projected wins is cheap; going from 75 to 80 is brutally expensive. That curve is why 82-0 is so rare even with an elite lineup — the last few wins demand a near-perfect roster.

sections.h2: Category thresholds: why one hole sinks you
paragraphs: On top of the curve, every category has a minimum threshold. If your lineup has essentially no rim protection or no playmaking, the engine caps your projected record regardless of how high your scoring total climbs. A balanced 78-4 roster beats a lopsided 90-points-but-zero-blocks roster every time. This models real basketball: a team that cannot defend the rim or run an offense loses games no matter how much it scores.

30 points per game in the fast-paced, high-scoring 1960s is not the same as 30 points in the 2020s. The engine deflates pace-inflated numbers from older decades and normalizes every stat line to a common baseline before summing, so a player is not rewarded just for playing in a high-tempo era. This keeps cross-decade lineups fair.
The fastest way to understand the scoring is to play. Spin a lineup, read the projected record and the 'biggest weakness' callout, then tweak your next run to plug that hole.

canYouGo.title: Can You Actually Go 82-0? Tips for an Undefeated Team
canYouGo.description: Can you really go 82-0 in the 82-0 challenge? Yes — but it's rare by design. Five concrete tips to maximize your projected record and chase the perfect undefeated season.
canYouGo.intro: Short answer: yes, but it is rare by design. The perfect season is reachable with the right lineup and a little luck. Here is how to give yourself the best shot.

paragraphs: Yes. A lineup that maximizes all five stat categories at once, with no glaring weakness, has a real shot at the perfect 82-0 season. But the engine's non-linear win curve makes the last few wins extremely costly, so even a stacked roster usually lands at 78-4 or 80-2. Hitting a true 82-0 should feel like making history — that is the whole point.

Do not chase points alone. The engine sums points, rebounds, assists, steals and blocks, and rewards balanced raw production. A lineup that is elite in scoring but empty in blocks or playmaking gets capped. Aim for the highest era-adjusted producers in every category, not five of the same archetype.

Every category has a floor. A starting five with zero rim protection or zero playmaking limits your ceiling no matter how much it scores. Before you lock a pick, ask which category your roster is thinnest in and whether this player helps it.

A 25-point scorer from the 2000s often beats a 30-point scorer from the 1960s after era adjustment, because the engine deflates pace-inflated older numbers. When two picks look close, the more recent, more efficient era usually wins.

You get one team skip and one era skip per game. A weak first-round roll is a hole you cannot climb out of later, so skip aggressively early. Hoarding both skips for round five usually means wasting them.

sections.h2: Can soccer or football actually go 82-0?
paragraphs: Not as a scoreline — goals are too hard to come by. The most lopsided official pro result ever was a freak 149-0 (a 2002 Madagascar protest match); a normal blowout rarely reaches double digits, and the Premier League's biggest margin is 9-0. But 82-0 was never really a scoreline. It is a perfect season: 82 games, 82 wins, zero losses — a basketball number, because an NBA regular season is 82 games long. Other sports have shorter seasons, so their 'perfect season' has a different number.

A Premier League season is 38 games, so soccer's version of the perfect undefeated season is 38-0. It is arguably harder than 82-0, because soccer draws so easily: Arsenal's legendary 2003-04 Invincibles went the whole season unbeaten and still only managed 26-12-0 — twelve draws short of a perfect 38-0. The 38-0 Challenge is the soccer edition of this exact game: spin Premier League clubs and eras, draft an XI of real legends, and chase the perfect season.

Want the international version? A World Cup run from the group stage to the final is seven matches, so a flawless tournament is 7-0. The 7-0 Challenge lets you build the greatest World Cup XI ever — mix legends from 1970 to 2026, link countrymen for chemistry, and chase a perfect 7-0 or survive a knockout gauntlet to lift the trophy.

If you searched 'football 82-0' meaning the NFL, the answer is 20-0. A modern Super Bowl run is 17 regular-season games plus three playoff rounds — win them all and you finish 20-0, something no team has done in the modern format (the 1972 Dolphins went 17-0 under the old schedule). The 20-0 Challenge drafts an NFL roster and simulates the whole run.

All four challenges share one idea: random team rolls, a draft built on real players, and a season simulation that decides whether your lineup survives undefeated. Pick your sport and chase the number — 82-0, 38-0, 20-0 or 7-0.

When the XI is complete, the simulation engine aggregates your squad's ratings — keeper, back line, midfield control, and firepower all weighted — and runs them through a non-linear 38-game win curve. One weak link caps your ceiling, exactly like a real title run.

sections.h2: 38-0 vs 82-0 vs 20-0: One Format, Three Sports
paragraphs: All three challenges run on the same core idea: random team draws, drafts built on real players, and a season simulation that decides whether your team survives undefeated. Football's version is the cruellest — eleven roster spots mean eleven chances to draft a passenger, and the gates punish a shaky keeper hardest. If you came chasing the 38-0 trend, the basketball original and the NFL edition are one click away on this site.

faqs.q: What is the 38-0 challenge?
faqs.a: The 38-0 challenge is a viral Premier League team builder game: a slot machine assigns random clubs and decades, you draft a starting XI of real legends, and a simulation projects whether your team could win all 38 games of a season.

faqs.q: Has any team ever gone 38-0?
faqs.a: No. Arsenal's 2003-04 Invincibles went unbeaten at 26-12-0, and Manchester City's 2017-18 centurions won 32 games. A perfect 38-win season has never happened in Premier League history.

faqs.q: Is 38-0 related to the 82-0 challenge?
faqs.a: Yes — 38-0 is the Premier League edition of the viral 82-0 basketball challenge (and its NFL cousin 20-0). Same slot-machine draws, real players, and a season simulation.

faqs.q: Can I play the 38-0 challenge for free?
faqs.a: Yes — it's playable right on this page, free, no download or account, in 7 languages. Spin clubs and eras, build your XI, and share your projected record.

twentyZero.title: 20-0 Challenge: Play the NFL Perfect Season Game
twentyZero.description: Play the viral 20-0 challenge. Spin random NFL teams and eras, draft a 9-man roster of football legends, and see if your team can win all 20 games to a perfect Super Bowl season.
twentyZero.intro: The NFL cousin of the viral 82-0 basketball challenge: spin the slot machine, draft a roster of football legends, and find out if they could win every game on the road to a perfect Super Bowl season. Play it right here.

paragraphs: A modern NFL champion plays a 17-game regular season plus three playoff games on the way to the Super Bowl (with a first-round bye). Win them all and you finish 20-0 — a perfect season. It has essentially never been done in the modern format: the 1972 Miami Dolphins famously went 17-0 under the old schedule, and the 2007 New England Patriots came one Super Bowl win short of perfection at 18-1. That gap between 'all-time great' and 'literally perfect' is what the number 20-0 stands for.
Just like 82-0 in basketball, 20-0 became shorthand for an impossible standard — a roster so stacked that it would not lose a single game all year.

The 20-0 challenge is a viral NFL roster builder in the same family as the 82-0 basketball challenge. The game spins up random all-time NFL franchises and you draft a 12-man roster of legends, position by position — quarterback, skill positions, line, and defense. Player pools draw on modern statistical history, so every pick carries real production numbers rather than vibes.

Once all twelve roster spots are filled, the simulation engine plays out a full 20-game season: seventeen regular-season games plus three playoff rounds. A perfect 20-0 run wins the Super Bowl, and you can share your final record and challenge friends to beat it. There is also a daily challenge format where everyone in the world gets the same spins and one attempt.

Both challenges run on the same core idea: random team draws, a draft built on real historical stats, and a simulation that decides whether your lineup survives an entire season undefeated. The differences come from the sports themselves. Basketball's 82-0 asks for five players and rewards balanced statistical categories across a long season; football's 20-0 asks for twelve roster spots and lives or dies on fewer, higher-stakes games — one bad simulated Sunday ends a perfect season.

If you came here chasing the 20-0 trend, you are in the right family of games. Our site hosts the basketball version: spin the slot machine, draft five legends from seven decades of history, and see if your lineup can do what no real team ever has.

faqs.q: What is the 20-0 challenge?
faqs.a: The 20-0 challenge is a viral NFL roster builder game where you draft a 12-man roster of football legends from randomly drawn teams, then a simulation plays out a 20-game season — 17 regular-season games plus 3 playoff rounds. Going 20-0 means a perfect Super Bowl-winning season.

faqs.q: Has any NFL team ever gone 20-0?
faqs.a: No. The 1972 Miami Dolphins finished 17-0 under the shorter schedule of their era, and the 2007 New England Patriots went 18-1, losing only the Super Bowl. A modern 20-0 perfect season has never happened.

faqs.q: Is 20-0 related to the 82-0 challenge?
faqs.a: Yes — 20-0 is the NFL version of the viral 82-0 basketball challenge. Both use random team draws, drafts built on real historical stats, and a season simulation that decides if your roster goes undefeated.

faqs.q: Can I play a 20-0 style game here?
faqs.a: This site hosts the basketball version of the format: the 82-0 challenge. Spin random teams and eras, draft five legends with real stats, and see if your lineup can finish a simulated season 82-0.

seventeenZero.title: 17-0 Challenge: Play the Perfect NFL Regular Season Game
seventeenZero.description: Play the 17-0 challenge free. Spin random NFL franchises and eras, draft a 9-man roster of football legends, and see if they can win all 17 games of a perfect regular season.
seventeenZero.intro: Since the NFL expanded to a 17-game schedule, 17-0 is the new name for a perfect regular season — and no team has ever pulled it off. Spin the slot machine, draft a roster of legends across three eras, and find out if your lineup can run the table. Play free below.

sections.h2: What Does 17-0 Mean in the NFL?
paragraphs: The NFL has played a 17-game regular season since 2021, and no team has finished it without a loss. The closest brushes with perfection came under older formats: the 1972 Miami Dolphins won every game they played — 14-0 in the regular season and 17-0 overall once the playoffs were done — and the 2007 New England Patriots went 16-0 before losing the Super Bowl. In today's format, 17-0 is the regular-season perfection nobody has reached.
That is what makes the number magnetic. Like 82-0 in basketball, 17-0 stands for a roster with no bad weeks — seventeen straight Sundays without a single slip.

The 17-0 challenge is a football roster builder in the same family as the viral 82-0 basketball challenge. The slot machine deals you a random all-time franchise and era, you draft one legend at a time into nine roster spots — quarterback, skill positions, the trenches, and the defense — and every player carries real production numbers from his era.

When the ninth spot is filled, the simulation engine projects a full 17-game regular season. Elite quarterback play matters most, but the engine punishes any soft spot on the roster: one weak position group is usually the difference between 17-0 and 15-2. Finish perfect and you can download a poster of your roster or share the record for friends to chase.

This site hosts both football challenges. The 17-0 version asks only for a perfect regular season; the 20-0 version adds a playoff run — three more wins on top, ending with the Super Bowl. The shorter slate makes 17-0 the friendlier target, but the same rule applies to both: a great roster gets you to 14 or 15 wins, and only a flawless one closes it out.
And if you want the original that started the family, the 82-0 basketball challenge is right here too — five legends, seven decades of history, eighty-two games without a loss.

faqs.q: Has any NFL team ever gone 17-0?
faqs.a: No. The 17-game schedule only began in 2021, and no team has finished it unbeaten. The 1972 Dolphins were perfect under a 14-game format (17-0 counting playoffs), and the 2007 Patriots went 16-0 before losing the Super Bowl.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the 17-0 and 20-0 challenges?
faqs.a: The roster building is the same — nine positions drafted from random franchise-and-era spins. The 17-0 challenge simulates only the 17-game regular season, while the 20-0 challenge adds three playoff wins and a Super Bowl on top, making it the harder perfect record.

faqs.q: How does the simulator decide my record?
faqs.a: Every player carries an overall rating from his era. The engine weighs each roster slot — quarterback heaviest, then the trenches and secondary — and projects wins on a steep curve, so one weak position group caps your ceiling no matter how strong the rest of the roster is.

faqs.q: Is the 17-0 challenge free to play?
faqs.a: Yes. It runs in the browser on desktop and mobile with no download or sign-up, and you can replay it as many times as you want.

nhl.title: 82-0 NHL Challenge: Play the Perfect Hockey Season Game
nhl.description: Play the 82-0 challenge, hockey edition. Spin random NHL franchises and eras, draft a six-man lineup of legends — forwards, defense, goalie — and see if they can win all 82 games.
nhl.intro: The NHL plays the exact same 82-game schedule as the NBA, so the 82-0 challenge translates to hockey perfectly. Spin the slot machine, draft a six-man lineup of legends from five decades — center, wingers, a defense pair, and a goalie — and find out if they could win every single night. Play free below.

sections.h2: What Would 82-0 Mean in the NHL?
paragraphs: An NHL regular season is 82 games — the same number as the NBA, which is why hockey fans keep typing '82-0 NHL' into search bars. No hockey team has come anywhere close: the best regular season ever, the 2022-23 Boston Bruins, finished 65-12-5, and the legendary 1976-77 Montreal Canadiens lost only eight times in a 80-game slate. Winning all 82 would mean surviving back-to-backs, road trips, hot goalies, and six months of bounces without one bad night.
That is exactly the fantasy this game simulates: not whether a great team can dominate, but whether a perfect lineup could literally never lose.

The slot machine deals you a random franchise-and-era combo — the 1980s Oilers, the 1990s Red Wings, the 2020s Avalanche — and you draft one player from that team into your six-man lineup: a center, both wingers, a defense pair, and a goalie. Five decades of legends are in the pool, from Gretzky and Bourque to Crosby, McDavid and Makar, each carrying a real statistical line from his era.

Fill all six slots and the engine projects your 82-game season. Goaltending and center play carry the heaviest weight, and the simulation punishes any passenger in the lineup — one weak slot is usually the difference between a Presidents' Trophy run and 82-0. You get one team re-roll and one era re-roll per draft, so spend them wisely.

Basketball's 82-0 is already absurd, but hockey adds two extra layers of chaos: a goalie can steal any game from either side, and one-goal margins decide almost half the league's nights. Even the deepest lineup in this game needs an elite goalie and zero soft spots before the engine will even consider handing out a perfect season — exactly the profile a real 82-0 team would need.

If you finish perfect, download the poster and share your lineup. And if you want to compare sports, the original basketball 82-0 challenge, the 17-0 NFL version and the rest of the family are all playable on this site.

faqs.q: Has any NHL team ever gone 82-0?
faqs.a: No — nothing close. The best NHL regular season by points percentage was the 1976-77 Montreal Canadiens (60-8-12), and the 2022-23 Boston Bruins set the wins record at 65. An 82-0 season has never happened in any major pro league.

faqs.q: How is the NHL version different from the basketball 82-0 challenge?
faqs.a: Same core loop — random team-and-era spins, a draft of legends, an 82-game simulation — but the lineup is six hockey slots (C, LW, RW, two D, G) instead of five basketball positions, and goaltending carries the most weight of any single slot.

faqs.q: Which eras and players are included?
faqs.a: Five decades of NHL history, from the 1980s to the 2020s, covering era-defining franchises like the Oilers dynasty, the 1990s Red Wings and Avalanche, the 2010s Blackhawks and Penguins, and today's stars like McDavid, MacKinnon and Makar.

faqs.q: Is the 82-0 NHL challenge free?
faqs.a: Yes. It runs in the browser on desktop and mobile with no download or sign-up, and you can replay as often as you like.

baseball162.title: 162-0 Challenge: Play the Baseball Perfect Season Game
baseball162.description: Play the 162-0 challenge. Draft an all-time MLB lineup of baseball legends across seven decades, then simulate a full 162-game season and see if your roster can do the impossible — go undefeated.
baseball162.intro: The baseball cousin of the viral 82-0 basketball challenge: spin all-time teams and eras, draft a nine-man diamond of legends, and find out if they could win all 162 games — the perfect season no MLB team has ever produced. Play it right here.

paragraphs: A modern MLB team plays 162 regular-season games. Win every single one and you finish 162-0 — a flawless season that has never come remotely close to happening. The best records in history still piled up dozens of losses: the 1906 Cubs went 116-36, the 2001 Mariners matched 116 wins at 116-46, and even those all-time juggernauts lost roughly one game in four. Across a 162-game grind, no roster has ever gone undefeated, and none ever will.
Just like 82-0 in basketball, 162-0 is shorthand for an impossible standard — a lineup so stacked it would not drop a single game across the longest season in major American sports.

The 162-0 challenge is a viral baseball roster builder in the same family as the 82-0 basketball challenge. The game spins up random all-time franchises and eras, and you draft a nine-player diamond — catcher, infield, outfield, and an ace on the mound — from legends spanning the 1960s to the 2020s. Every pick carries a real all-time reputation, so you are weighing dynasties and decades, not vibes.

Once your nine are set, the simulation engine plays out a full 162-game season against a league of all-time opponents. A perfect 162-0 run is the holy grail; fall short and you will still chase the pennant, a division title, or the best record in baseball. Share your final record and challenge friends to beat it.

Both challenges run on the same core idea: random team draws, a draft built on all-time greats, and a simulation that decides whether your lineup survives an entire season undefeated. The differences come from the sports themselves. Basketball's 82-0 asks for five players over 82 games; baseball's 162-0 asks for a full nine-man diamond and the longest season in sports — twice the games, twice the variance, and a far steeper climb to perfection.

If you came here chasing the 162-0 trend, you are in the right family of games. Spin the diamond, draft your legends, and see if your lineup can do what no real team ever has — then try the original 82-0 basketball version too.

faqs.q: What is the 162-0 challenge?
faqs.a: The 162-0 challenge is a viral baseball roster builder where you draft a nine-player all-time lineup from randomly drawn teams and eras, then a simulation plays out a full 162-game MLB season. Going 162-0 means a flawless, undefeated regular season.

faqs.q: Has any MLB team ever gone 162-0?
faqs.a: No — not even close. The best records ever are the 1906 Cubs (116-36) and 2001 Mariners (116-46), and both still lost dozens of games. A 162-0 perfect season has never happened and is considered impossible over so long a schedule.

faqs.q: Is 162-0 related to the 82-0 challenge?
faqs.a: Yes — 162-0 is the baseball version of the viral 82-0 basketball challenge. Both use random team draws, drafts built on all-time greats, and a season simulation that decides if your roster goes undefeated.

faqs.q: How do I play the 162-0 baseball game?
faqs.a: Spin random teams and eras, draft your nine-man diamond of baseball legends, then simulate the 162-game season. Try to balance hitting, defense, and pitching to chase the impossible perfect record — and share your result to challenge friends.

teamBuilder.title: Custom Lineup Builder — Pick Any Five NBA Legends, No Random Draws
teamBuilder.description: Build any all-time five from 420 legends across seven decades — no spins, no luck. Choose a playstyle, simulate a full 82-game season, and settle lineup debates with numbers.
teamBuilder.intro: No spins, no luck of the draw — browse the full pool of 420 legends, hand-pick any five, and simulate the season. The tool for settling all-time lineup debates.

sections.h2: How This Differs From the 82-0 Challenge
paragraphs: The main 82-0 Challenge deals you random team-and-era combinations, and the skill is drafting well under constraints you didn't choose. This page removes the randomness entirely: every one of the 420 players in the database is available from the first click. Search by name, filter by decade or franchise, and place anyone into any position he actually played.

Because there is no constraint, lineups built here don't post to the leaderboard — a hand-picked dream team would swamp every ranked run in seconds. Think of this page as the film room and the home page as the game: test a theory here, then see how far the same instincts carry you when the spins decide what you get.

Could a starting five of prime Jordan, Magic, Bird, Duncan, and Shaq really go 82-0? Does an all-1990s lineup beat an all-2020s lineup once the pace difference is adjusted away? Can any team survive a full season with no true center? These are the arguments this tool was built for — construct both sides and let the simulation answer.

Every stat line is era-adjusted before it enters the engine, so a 1960s rebounding number doesn't inflate against a modern one. That means cross-era teams are compared on a level floor — the debates stay about the players, not the pace of their decade.

The season engine is identical to the main challenge: your five players' era-adjusted totals in points, rebounds, assists, steals, and blocks are measured against a benchmark in each category, combined into a weighted strength score, and pushed through a non-linear win curve where each extra win costs more than the last. One glaring hole caps the projected record no matter how strong the rest of the roster is, and even an elite, balanced five still needs the final luck roll to land the perfect 82-0. See the How It's Calculated page for the full breakdown.

sevenZero.title: 7-0 Game: World Cup All-Time Dream Team Builder
sevenZero.description: Build the greatest World Cup XI ever. Mix legends from 1970 to 2026, stack countrymen for chemistry, run the knockout gauntlet, and chase a perfect 7–0. Free, no sign-up.
sevenZero.h1: 7-0 Game — All-Time World Cup Dream Team
sevenZero.intro: This is the deepest 7-0 builder we make: pull a single nation or an open World All-Stars pool, drop real players from eight decades into your formation, link countrymen for chemistry, then either chase a single flawless 7–0 or survive a four-round knockout gauntlet to lift the trophy.

sections.h2: World All-Stars: the cross-nation dream team
paragraphs: Most 7-0 games lock you to one country. This one adds a World All-Stars mode that throws open the doors: a single pool can hand you Pelé, Maradona, Cruyff and Zidane to line up in the same eleven. You are no longer building Brazil's best or France's best — you are building football's best, full stop.

But raw ratings are not enough. Chemistry rewards placing countrymen next to each other on the pitch, so the perfect All-Stars side is a balancing act between star power and national links. A team of eleven loners from eleven nations will look terrifying on paper and misfire on grass.

Single-match mode is the classic chase for one perfect 7–0. The gauntlet is the long road: your dream team must win four straight knockout rounds — group, round of 16, semi-final and final — against opponents that get stronger every step. Lose once and you are out; win all four and you are champions.

Because you keep the same squad through the bracket, the gauntlet rewards a deep, well-built eleven over a flat-track bully. You can tweak your line-up between rounds, so reading the next opponent and shifting your tactical style becomes part of the game.

Alongside the modern 2018, 2022 and 2026 squads, we added hand-picked legendary editions: Brazil 1970 and 2002, Argentina 1986, the Netherlands of 1974, West Germany 1990, France 1998, Italy 1982, England 1966, Spain 2010 and Uruguay 1950. Draw one of these and you are building with the players who actually defined the World Cup.
It means a single roll can send you eight decades back or drop you into a projected 2026 side — and in All-Stars mode, all of those eras share one player pool.

faqs.q: How is this different from the standalone 7-0 Game?
faqs.a: This in-site edition adds four things the standalone does not have: a cross-nation World All-Stars mode, a four-round knockout gauntlet, a chemistry system that rewards linking countrymen, and hand-built legendary squads from 1950 to 2010.

faqs.q: What is a perfect 7–0?
faqs.a: 7–0 is the flawless scoreline. To earn it you need a high-rated eleven, every player in a position they truly fit, strong chemistry in All-Stars mode, and a tactical style that suits your squad.

faqs.q: How does chemistry work?
faqs.a: In World All-Stars mode, each player links with their on-pitch neighbours. Neighbours from the same nation raise chemistry; isolated players lower it. Higher chemistry boosts your attack and defence, so clustering countrymen matters as much as raw ratings.

faqs.q: What is the gauntlet?
faqs.a: A knockout run of four rounds with rising difficulty. The same dream team must win all four — group, round of 16, semi-final and final — to be crowned champions. You can adjust your line-up between rounds.

faqs.q: Are the players and ratings real?
faqs.a: Player names are real, era-appropriate footballers and ratings are believable approximations for entertainment. This is an independent fan project, not affiliated with FIFA, any federation or club.

faqs.q: Is it free and multilingual?
faqs.a: Yes. It is completely free, needs no account, runs in your browser, and is available in English, 中文, 日本語, 한국어, Español, Français and Deutsch. Your stats are saved locally on your device.

capMode.title: 82-0 Salary Cap Mode — The Strategic NBA Draft Game
capMode.description: A more strategic 82-0: build an NBA starting five under a fixed salary cap and chase an undefeated 82-game season without an unlimited superteam.
capMode.intro: A more strategic 82-0 NBA draft turned gauntlet. Every player has a price; you start with a loose budget and roll-and-pick your five. Go 82-0 and the budget tightens for the next level — how deep can you climb before a perfect season is unaffordable?

paragraphs: Cap Mode is the strategic twist on 82-0. Instead of an unlimited all-time superteam, every player carries a price and you build your starting five under a fixed salary cap. Spend it all on three megastars and you will have nothing left for the other two slots; spread it too thin and your team rating sags. The fun is in the trade-off.

Each run is a gauntlet. You begin at Level 1 with a generous salary cap. Hit Spin to roll a random team and era — but only the players you can still afford show up in the list. Pick one, drop them onto a court position, and their price comes off your cap.

Keep rolling and drafting until all five spots are filled, then watch the 82-game season simulate. Finish 82-0 and you clear the level: the budget tightens for the next one and your streak continues. Fall short of a perfect record and the run ends — your score is how many levels you cleared. The game always reserves enough cap for your remaining slots, so you can never spend yourself into a corner.

Every player is priced from the same production score the engine uses to rate your team — points, rebounds, assists, steals and blocks, adjusted for era. Prices run from about 5 for role players up to the low-30s for the all-time greats. You roll for teams and eras like classic 82-0, but only players you can still afford appear — and the game always reserves enough for your remaining spots, so you can't spend yourself into a dead end.

It plays as a gauntlet: you start with a generous budget and, every time you go 82-0, the budget tightens for the next level. A season that falls short of 82-0 ends the run, and how deep you climbed is your score. Any budget left unspent becomes a small efficiency bonus to your team rating.

A common winning shape is two or three priced-up stars plus cheap, efficient role players who fill the gaps. Because the engine punishes any single weak category, do not ignore defense — steals and blocks are baked into both the price and the win curve, so a cheap rim protector can be better value than another scorer.
Watch your positions too: a versatile guard or forward who fits multiple slots gives you more freedom to spend where it matters.

Cap Mode seasons are tagged on the global leaderboard so cap builders stand apart from classic runs. Climb the board by maximizing your team rating under budget — and if you go 82-0, the cap you left on the table is your edge over everyone else who did the same.

paragraphs: The classic 82-0 challenge hands you random teams and eras to draft from. Challenge Filters give you control instead — reshape the draftable pool and the difficulty to make a harder, more deliberate run at the perfect season. Each filter also tags your leaderboard entry, so a No MVPs 82-0 reads very differently from an everyone-allowed one.

sections.h2: How to play the 82-0 Challenge Filters
paragraphs: Pick a filter to reshape the draft. For One Franchise or One Decade, choose your team or era first. Then play 82-0 the usual way — spin a team and era, pick a player for each of the five court positions, and simulate the season.

Each filter changes which players you can draft and how hard a perfect season is, and your result is tagged on the global leaderboard by filter, so a No MVPs 82-0 sits apart from an everyone-allowed one. Prefer a single mode on its own page? Each filter also has a dedicated challenge page.

Salary Cap: a gauntlet where you roll your five under a budget that tightens every time you go 82-0 — the most strategic mode. No MVPs: the priciest all-time greats are banned, so you win without the icons. One Franchise: draft only from a single team's all-time roster. One Decade: lock the whole draft to one era of NBA history. Random Era: the game picks your decade for you. Hard Mode: a steeper win curve where even stacked rosters drop a few more games.

Hard Mode and Salary Cap are the toughest tests of a true 82-0. One Franchise and One Decade are medium — your ceiling depends on the team or era you pick. If you are new, start with Classic, then add filters one at a time as you learn which rosters actually survive 82 games.

noMvps.title: 82-0 No MVPs Challenge — Win Without the All-Time Greats
noMvps.description: Take the 82-0 NBA challenge with the priciest all-time greats banned. Build an undefeated starting five from role players and underrated stars.
noMvps.intro: The hardest bragging rights in basketball: go 82-0 without a single MVP-tier superstar. The ~35 priciest all-time greats are off the board — win with role players, glue guys and underrated stars instead.

sections.h2: What counts as an MVP here?
paragraphs: No MVPs mode bans the roughly 35 most valuable players in the pool — the all-time scoring and rebounding giants the engine prices highest. Everyone else is fair game, which means you are building from very good players rather than legends. It is the same roll-and-draft 82-0, just without the easy buttons.

Hit Spin to roll a team and era, then pick a player for each court position — exactly like the classic 82-0 game. The only difference is that the roughly 35 priciest all-time greats are removed from every list, so you are building from very good players instead of legends. Fill all five spots, simulate the 82-game season, and submit your record to the No MVPs leaderboard.

Balance wins it. The engine punishes any single weak category, so spread your production across scoring, rebounding, assists, steals and blocks. Cheap rim protectors and high-assist guards carry more weight than another mid-volume scorer, and a versatile forward who covers two positions buys you flexibility. Hit every category and even a star-less five can chase a perfect season.

Yes, but it is hard. Without elite scorers and rebounders to carry you, a perfect season demands a genuinely balanced five — solid in scoring, rebounding, assists, steals and blocks all at once. The win curve punishes any single weak category, so the trick is value: cheap defenders, efficient playmakers and versatile wings that cover a hole the stars would normally paper over. Pull it off and an 82-0 with no MVPs is one of the toughest brags on the leaderboard.

oneTeam.title: 82-0 One Franchise Challenge — One Team, Every Era
oneTeam.description: Build an undefeated 82-0 NBA starting five using only one franchise's all-time roster — Lakers, Celtics, Bulls, Spurs and more.
oneTeam.intro: Loyalty mode. Draft your entire 82-0 starting five from a single franchise's all-time roster — every Laker, every Celtic, every Bull across the decades. Can your team go undefeated on its own?

paragraphs: Pick a franchise from the menu and every roll in the draft is locked to that team — but across all eras of its history, so a 60s legend can line up next to a modern star. Only franchises with enough all-time depth to fill a balanced five are offered, so the draft never dead-ends.

Choose a franchise from the dropdown above the game. Every time you Spin, the team is locked to that franchise but the era changes, so you draft across its whole history. Pick a player for each of the five court positions, simulate the season, and see whether one club's all-time talent is enough to go undefeated. Switch the franchise any time to start a fresh run.

The storied, deep franchises — the Lakers, Celtics, Bulls, Spurs and Warriors — field the most complete all-time fives and give you the best shot at a perfect season. Picking a younger or thinner franchise is the real challenge: you may be strong in one or two categories but exposed elsewhere, and the win curve will find the hole.

The deepest all-time rosters give you the most room: the Lakers, Celtics, Bulls, Spurs and Warriors can each field a complete, balanced five from their history. Younger or thinner franchises are the real test — you might be loaded at one position and exposed at another, and the win curve will find the gap. Part of the fun is discovering which clubs can carry a perfect season on their own and which fall just short.

oneDecade.title: 82-0 One Decade Challenge — One Era, One Perfect Season
oneDecade.description: Lock your 82-0 NBA draft to a single decade of basketball history — the 60s, 80s, 90s, 2000s and beyond — and chase an undefeated season.
oneDecade.intro: Pick an era and live in it. Your whole 82-0 starting five must come from one decade of NBA history — the gritty 90s, the pace-and-space 2010s, your call. Which decade had the firepower to go undefeated?

paragraphs: Choose a decade and every team you roll is from that era — you build a five frozen in one moment of NBA history. The engine still adjusts each player's raw stats for the era they played in, so a 60s scoring title is not worth the same as a 90s one; the decade you pick shapes both who is available and how their numbers translate.

Choose a decade from the dropdown above the game. Every team you Spin comes from that era, so your whole five is frozen in one moment of NBA history. Pick a player for each court position, simulate the 82-game season, and find out which decade had the depth to go perfect. Change the decade any time to try another era.

Every decade has a path to 82-0, but they win differently. The 90s and 2000s are stacked with two-way wings and dominant centers; the 80s bring elite playmaking and scoring; the 2010s and 2020s lean on shooting and switchable defense. Part of the fun is finding which era's strengths line up with the categories the win curve rewards.

Every era has a path, but they win differently. The 1990s and 2000s are stacked with two-way wings and dominant centers; the 1980s bring elite playmaking and scoring; the 2010s and 2020s lean on shooting and switchable defense. Because the engine adjusts each player's stats for their era, the decade you lock in shapes both who is available and how their numbers translate — so the strongest decade is often the one whose strengths line up with the categories the win curve rewards.

hardMode.title: 82-0 Hard Mode — The Toughest Perfect-Season Challenge
hardMode.description: 82-0 with a steeper win curve. Even a stacked all-time starting five drops a few more games — only the very best rosters survive undefeated.
hardMode.intro: For players who find the perfect season too easy. Hard Mode steepens the win curve and tightens the 82-0 luck gate, so even a stacked all-time five drops a few more games. Only the very best rosters survive.

paragraphs: Hard Mode keeps the same all-time player pool but bends the math against you: the non-linear win curve gets a steeper exponent, so the same roster wins fewer games, and the gate for a true 82-0 is tightened. A five that cruises to 80-2 in the standard game might land at 76-6 here.

It plays exactly like the classic 82-0 game — spin a team and era, pick a player for each of the five court positions, and simulate the season — but the math is harsher. The win curve is steeper and the gate for a perfect record is tighter, so the same roster wins fewer games. Build a five with no weak categories and you might just survive 82-0.

There is no margin for a weak category. Maximize scoring, rebounding, assists, steals and blocks all at once — any single hole drags the curve down harder than in the standard game. Prioritize two-way players who pad the defensive stats, and use your team and era re-rolls to chase the exact pieces your five is missing.

It is, but only for the very best rosters. A five that cruises to 80-2 in the standard game might land at 76-6 in Hard Mode, and the luck gate for a true 82-0 is tightened on top of that. There is no room for a weak category — you need elite, balanced production everywhere, plus a little luck. That is exactly why a Hard Mode 82-0 is the most impressive perfect season you can post.

eraMode.title: 82-0 Era Mode — Build an All-Time Team Across Every Era
eraMode.description: The cross-era 82-0 challenge, like EraBall: draft one legend from each decade — 1960s to today — and see if your all-time starting five can go a perfect 82-0.
eraMode.intro: Looking for EraBall or the era ball 82-0 game? Era Mode is the cross-era draft: every pick must come from a different decade, so your starting five spans the whole history of basketball — a legend from the 1960s, 70s, 80s, 90s, 2000s, 2010s and 2020s. Build the ultimate all-time team and chase a perfect, undefeated season.

paragraphs: Era Mode is a cross-era twist on the 82-0 challenge. In the classic game the spin can hand you the same decade twice; in Era Mode, once you draft a player from a decade that era is locked out, so your finished five always spans the eras — one legend per decade. It is the all-time, every-era team-building fantasy that fans of EraBall and the era ball 82-0 game come looking for, with the same undefeated-season payoff.

It plays like the classic 82-0 game — spin a team and era, then pick a player for one of the five court positions — with a single extra rule: every pick must come from a decade you have not used yet. The slot machine automatically skips eras already on your roster, so by the time your five is set it spans the decades. Then simulate the season and see how close your cross-era all-time team comes to a perfect 82-0.

Both are about drafting an all-time NBA roster across every era. EraBall leans on picking a coach and simulating the playoffs; Era Mode keeps the pure 82-0 question — can your five go undefeated across a full 82-game regular season — and adds the one-legend-per-decade rule so the team genuinely spans history. If you love building cross-era dream teams, Era Mode is the fastest way to chase a perfect record.

Spread your strengths across the decades. Because you cannot stack two players from the same era, plan which decade you want each position to come from — grab a dominant 1960s or 70s big for rebounding and blocks, a 1990s or 2000s wing for scoring, and a modern playmaker for assists and steals. Use your team and era re-rolls to find the exact piece a decade is missing, and keep every category balanced — one weak stat still drags an all-time five short of 82-0.

lebronMode.title: LeBron Mode: Build an 82-0 Team Around LeBron James
lebronMode.description: LeBron James is locked into your lineup — Cavs LeBron, Heat LeBron or Lakers LeBron. Draft the other four legends around him and chase the perfect 82-0 season.
lebronMode.intro: The King is already on your roster. Every run locks a random era of LeBron James into the five — young Cleveland LeBron, Miami Big-Three LeBron or Lakers LeBron — and your job is to draft the four legends around him that finish 82-0. His other era cards leave the pool, so there is exactly one LeBron on the floor.

paragraphs: LeBron Mode is the 82-0 challenge with the first pick made for you. When a run starts, the game deals one of LeBron's four era cards — 2000s Cavaliers, Big-Three Heat, return-to-Cleveland or 2020s Lakers — straight into a forward slot. From there the classic draft takes over: spin random franchise-and-era combos and fill the remaining four positions, with one team re-roll and one era re-roll to spend.

Because each version of LeBron carries different numbers — the Miami card is the most efficient scorer, the late Cleveland card the best playmaker — the right supporting cast changes from run to run. Replay and the game hands you a different LeBron to build around.

sections.h2: Can LeBron Carry a Perfect Season?
paragraphs: LeBron's real teams won four championships but never came close to a perfect regular season — the 73-win 2015-16 Warriors beat his Cavaliers to the record, and Cleveland answered in the Finals instead. The simulation tells the same story: one superstar covers a lot of nights, but 82-0 demands that all five categories stay elite, so your four picks have to plug rebounding, rim protection and secondary scoring around him.

That is the fun of the mode: everyone gets the same head start, and the leaderboard settles who built the best supporting cast. If you'd rather start from scratch, the classic 82-0 challenge and the other modes are one click away.
